title: Representation Entanglement for Generation: Training Diffusion Transformers

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper gives s(x,t) = σ_t^{-1} · (α_t v(x,t) - α̇_t x) / (α_t σ̇_t - α̇_t σ_t). Deriving from v = α̇_t 𝔼[x∗] + σ̇_t 𝔼[ε] and x = α_t 𝔼[x∗] + σ_t 𝔼[ε] shows that 𝔼[ε] = (α_t v - α̇_t x) / (σ̇_t α_t - α̇_t σ_t). The score is s = -σ_t^{-1} 𝔼[ε], so a minus sign is required. The paper's expression is off by a sign.

Abstract: 'SiT-L/2 + REG trained for 400K iterations achieves comparable FID scores to SiT-XL/2 + REPA trained for 4M iterations.' Introduction: 'SiT-L/2 + REPA trained for 400K iterations achieves performance comparable to SiT-XL/2 + REPA trained for 4M iterations.' In Table 1, SiT-L/2 + REG 400K FID=9.8, SiT-XL/2 + REPA 4M FID=5.9; SiT-L/2 + REPA 400K FID=9.7. Neither is 'comparable' (differences of ~4 FID).

Text: 'For smaller models, SiT-B/2 + REG outperforms SiT-B/2 + REPA by 9.2 FID points and surpasses SiT-L/2 trained for 400K iterations by 3.6 points.' Table 1 shows SiT-B/2 + REPA 24.4, SiT-B/2+REG 21.8 (difference 2.6, not 9.2). SiT-L/2 at 400K is 18.8, which is lower (better) than REG's 21.8, so REG does not surpass it.

Caption states: 'All metrics report the average and standard deviation over three independent runs with different random seeds.' No standard deviations are shown in the table; only single values appear.

Table 1 reports SiT-B/2 + REG 400K FID 21.8, SiT-L/2 + REG 400K FID 9.8, SiT-XL/2 + REG 400K FID 5.6, 4M FID 3.3. Table 3 reports SiT-B/2 + REG 400K FID 15.22 with same settings. Table 9 reports SiT-L/2 + REG 400K FID 4.6, SiT-XL/2 + REG 400K FID 3.4, 4M FID 1.8. The FID values are inconsistent across these tables.

Text: 'DINOv2-B delivers optimal performance, achieving a 19.18% FID reduction and 35.86% IS improvement.' Actual numbers: SiT-B/2 FID 33.0, with entanglement 29.9 → reduction (33.0-29.9)/33.0 = 9.4%, not 19.18%. IS: baseline 43.7, entanglement 52.3 → improvement 19.7%, not 35.86%.

Table 2 compares 'SiT-XL/2' and 'DiT-XL/2' baselines (without CFG, FID 2.06, 2.27) against '+REG (ours)' with FID 2.15–1.34, reportedly using CFG (guidance interval). The comparison mixes CFG and non-CFG results, making REG appear spuriously better; the table does not clearly state that REG uses CFG while baselines do not.

Table 2 reports SiT-XL/2 + REG 80 epochs FID 2.15, 160 epochs 1.75, 480 epochs 1.38, 800 epochs 1.34. Table 8 gives for identical epochs: 1.86, 1.59, 1.40, 1.36. The numbers conflict, indicating inconsistent reporting of the same experimental condition.
